en.headline: Police receive over 700 reports of unauthorised iPhone purchases worth HK$14.7m
en.dek: Officers said electronic reports from Saturday to Sunday involved suspected credit-card theft for online smartphone buys, with the largest single case about HK$114,000; no arrests yet.
body: Police said on Sunday they had received more than 700 reports of suspected unauthorised credit-card transactions used to buy smartphones online, with a combined value of about HK$14.7 million.

The electronic reports arrived between Saturday and Sunday after pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro series opened on Saturday evening. The largest single case involved roughly HK$114,000. Police classified the cases as obtaining property by deception and said no one had been arrested pending further investigation.

Several banks, including HSBC, Hang Seng and Standard Chartered, said they were examining the transactions and would process chargebacks under card-scheme rules where appropriate. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority reminded cardholders to check statements and freeze cards immediately if suspicious activity appears.

zh.headline: 警方接逾700宗疑盜用信用卡購智能電話報案 涉款約1470萬
zh.dek: 電子報案中心周六至周日接獲超過700人報案，指信用卡疑被盜用於網上購買智能電話，最大一宗約11.4萬元，暫無人被捕。
body: 警方表示，電子報案中心於9月12日至13日接獲超過700人報案，懷疑信用卡被盜用於網上購買智能電話，涉款約1470萬元，最大一宗案件涉及約11.4萬元。
案件暫列「以欺騙手段取得財產」，暫未有人被捕。事件發生在iPhone 18 Pro系列周六晚開放預購之後，多名市民收到銀行短訊通知有未經授權的Apple Store交易。
滙豐、恒生及渣打等多間銀行表示正調查相關交易，並會在適用情況下按信用卡組織規則啟動退單機制。金管局提醒市民核對交易紀錄，遇有懷疑即時停用信用卡。
